title: Appendix A — Symbolic Action in a Poem by Keats
folder: Burke - Symbolic Action in a Poem by Keats
role: First of four Appendix essays (re-published earlier journal essays gathered as applied-dramatism case studies). Burke offers a sustained reading of Keats's 'Ode on a Grecian Urn', tracking how the poem's act (the speaker addressing the urn), scene (the urn-as-scene-of-frozen-action), agents (the figures depicted on the urn), and purpose (the truth/beauty closing identity) interlock. Demonstrates the 'symbolic action' method: a lyric is read as a strategic motive-statement deploying terministic resources, not merely as expression. Phase 3 will use this essay as the methodological template for the dissertation's empirical-adaptation chapter at single-text scale. The chapter quotes the Ode in segments and develops the analysis around the quoted blocks — Phase 2 must preserve verse line-breaks in chunking.
